The search for 'The Northern Lights' is at an all-time high. As per Pickyourtrail, a travel platform offering customised international tour packages and trip planning services, recently shared that Northern lights demand surged 214% YoY, reflecting growing interest in experience-led winter holidays. However, this shouldn't come as a surprise, as every traveller wants to experience Aurora Borealis (scientific name for the Northern Lights). It is something you will find on every traveler's bucket list.

In recent years, aurora chasing has turned into a global travel phenomenon, driven by viral night-sky photography, peak solar activity cycles, and travelers seeking rare, bucket-list natural wonders. It is said that the best time to see the Northern Lights is between October and March.

7 best places in the world to see the Northern Lights

1. Tromsø, Norway

Located at 69°N latitude in the heart of the Arctic auroral oval, Tromsø is widely regarded as the Northern Lights capital of Europe. Thanks to the warm Gulf Stream, its coastal climate remains surprisingly mild compared to inland sub-zero locations. Positioned directly under the primary geomagnetic oval, Tromsø experiences auroral activity almost every clear night from mid-September to early April. If you're planning a trip here to see northern lights, you must book do so via an Arctic fjord cruise, or ride the Fjellheisen Cable Car to Mount Storsteinen for panoramic city-and-aurora views.

2. Abisko, Sweden

Nestled inside Swedish Lapland, Abisko National Park boasts one of the most reliable record rates of aurora sightings in the world. Abisko sits in a unique microclimate created by surrounding mountains and Lake Torneträsk, creating a persistent "blue hole" of clear sky even when neighboring coastal areas are overcast. For a wholesome experience, take the chairlift up Mount Nuolja to the Aurora Sky Station, an elevated observatory built specifically for dark-sky stargazing.

3. Yellowknife, Northwest Territories, Canada

This remote Canadian capital sits on flat tundra with unobstructed horizon-to-horizon views. Yellowknife experiences auroral activity on over 240 nights per year due to its flat geography, low coastal moisture, and positioning right under the northern auroral zone. In fact, this place offers the longest viewing window from mid-August to late April. Stay at Aurora Village, where you can watch the lights dance across the sky from heated teepees, or custom glass dome cabins.

4. Fairbanks, Alaska, USA

Fairbanks is North America’s premier aurora destination. Located just south of the Arctic Circle, it balances Arctic wilderness with high-end travel infrastructure. Statistics show that staying in Fairbanks for 3 consecutive nights yields a 4-in-5 (80%+) chance of witnessing an aurora display, provided skies are clear. The best window for viewing the northern lights is between late August to late April. To enjoy the experience even more, soak in the open-air outdoor mineral pools at Chena Hot Springs while the green lights dance overhead in sub-zero air.

5. Luosto & Inari, Finnish Lapland

Finnish Lapland combines world-class aurora viewing with luxury Arctic hospitality. Regions around Lake Inari and Luosto offer pristine dark skies away from major urban hubs. Northern Finland records aurora displays roughly 200 nights a year (roughly 2 out of every 3 clear nights in winter). What you can do is sleep in a heated glass igloo equipped with automated "Aurora Alarm" notifications that wake you when geomagnetic activity spikes.

6. Snæfellsnes Peninsula & South Coast, Iceland

Iceland is unique because the entire island nation sits directly within the active aurora belt. This means you can potentially spot the lights anywhere across the country. Dark, uninhabited volcanic terrain allows travelers to step just minutes outside small coastal towns into total darkness. Frame your photography with iconic volcanic landmarks like Kirkjufell Mountain, or the icebergs floating in the Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon.

7. Kangerlussuaq & Ilulissat, Greenland

For travelers seeking raw Arctic wilderness without light pollution, Greenland offers unmatched clarity. Kangerlussuaq enjoys over 300 clear nights a year due to a stable inland desert microclimate, giving it one of the highest success rates for aurora chasers anywhere in the Arctic. For a standout experience, watch the curtain of green light illuminate giant icebergs floating in Disko Bay near the UNESCO-listed Ilulissat Icefjord.
